title: A missing theorem on dual spaces

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: It states 'J² = I (since (J²)* = -I)'. Since J* = L_i and L_i² = -I, the dual of J² is -I, so J² = -I, not I.
The remark defines ρ: E†† → Y** by i_E(x) ↦ i_Y(x) and says it is the isometry μ from the proof. But μ in Lemma 1.3 maps Y** → E†† and takes i_Y(y) to i_E(y), so ρ = μ^{-1}, not μ.
The statement says the isomorphism 'takes i_F(x) to i_F††(x) for x ∈ X' (X undefined). The map should take i_E(x) to i_F(x) for x ∈ E, as the later proof confirms.

The theorem gives only hypotheses and then the proof begins; no conclusions are stated. The proof refers to item (1) and later to 'the proof of (2) above', but those items are absent from the statement.
It cites 'the Paulsen trick in the remark below Corollary 4.5', but no such remark exists; the remark after Corollary 4.5 concerns analogous results for TROs and operator algebras.

It writes Q|_{S(Y)} = I|_{S(Y)} although Q is defined only on the real Paulsen system S_R(Y**). The complex Paulsen system S(Y) is not a subspace of S_R(Y**), so the restriction is undefined; presumably S_R(Y) was intended.

It asserts L_i is not a real Banach space centralizer of a complex Banach space. Under the standard centralizer condition ||I+αT||=1+o(α), for T=iI one has ||I+α iI||=√(1+α²)=1+O(α²), so L_i is a centralizer.
The paper cites numerous numbered references such as [1], [2], [4], [5], [6], [12], [22], [23], [24], [25], etc., but no reference list/bibliography is included.
